chunks: With this chain of transmission, from ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥasan, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Abī Najrān, from Ṣafwān ibn Yaḥyā, from ʿĪṣ ibn al-Qāsim, who said:
I asked Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about the leftover water of a menstruating woman,
He said: Perform wudu (ablution) with it, and perform wudu (ablution) from the leftover water of the junub when she is trustworthy, and she washes her hand before putting it into the vessel.
And the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم used to perform ghusl, he and ʿĀʾishah, in one vessel, and they would bathe together.

key_terms.الْإِنَاءَ: the vessel or container of water
key_terms.الْجُنُبِ: a person in a state requiring ghusl due to janabah
key_terms.سُؤْرِ: leftover water or remnant from which someone has drunk or used
key_terms.مَأْمُونَةً: trusted, such that impurity is not feared from her handling

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to perform wudu (ablution) with the leftover water of a menstruating woman or a junub?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses the ruling on using leftover water from a menstruating woman and a junub for wudu (ablution). It indicates permissibility when impurity is not feared, and it supports this with an example from the practice of the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم.
